task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (WF-02 Step 2c) PASSED with no BLOCKER -- full findings in handoffs/WF02-REQ198-20260830/security-review-req198-findings.md. REQ-198 adds a function-call syntax and 8 pure builtins (length, lower, upper, trim, contains, startsWith, endsWith, coalesce) to lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex atop REQ-197's arithmetic/comparison grammar, per the approved design lib/letflow/design/req198-expr-builtin-functions.md. Independently re-verified (not trusting ELIXIR-DEV's self-report): mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean, mix format --check-formatted clean, purity grep (Repo./Logger./DateTime./System.os_time/System.system_time/HTTPoison./Req./File./:rand./:crypto.) zero matches against the real current file, mix test test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs 148/148 passing, mix letflow.lint_handoffs 0 new violations. Diff scope confirmed via git diff main...HEAD --stat: only lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex, test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs, the design doc, and handoff/registry/status-index bookkeeping changed -- no migration, no route, no config/secret handling. Directly executed (mix run --no-start, not just reading test names) to confirm now()/date_add(a,b)/frobnicate(1) genuinely fail to parse as {:trailing_input, ...} rather than being silently accepted, and that a wrong-arity call (length(a,b)) safely collapses to false via evaluate_condition/2's catch-false. Confirmed the closed-whitelist mapping (identifier_token/1, identifier_token_kv/1) is a literal 8-clause dispatch with zero String.to_atom/1 or String.to_existing_atom/1 introduced. Confirmed contains/startsWith/endsWith use plain String.contains?/2, String.starts_with?/2, String.ends_with?/2 (no Regex, no ReDoS surface) and @unsupported_call_markers has zero diff churn. Now handing to REVIEWER for the idiom/OTP/scope-creep/decision-record-consistency gate (WF-02 Step 2d) -- please review naming/style consistency with REQ-197's established conventions (the design doc's stated intent to mirror REQ-197's dual parse_primary/parse_primary_p, parse_call_args/parse_call_args_p pattern), the eval_args/check_arity/apply_builtin decomposition, and whether the new :wrong_arity eval-error tag and :call AST node fit this module's existing error-tag/AST conventions cleanly.

Confirm no scope creep beyond the approved design doc's §1-§8 (8 builtins, call syntax, closed whitelist -- nothing else).

Confirm supervision/process-isolation is not implicated (this module is a pure function library, no GenServer/gen_statem changes) -- state explicitly that this check is trivially satisfied given the diff's shape.
Confirm consistency with REQ-197's decision-record precedent (now()/date_add()/date_diff() permanent exclusion, ASCII-only casing fidelity decision) -- no silent re-litigation of either.
